items.readable_text:
Content:
When the [MATH: n]th term [MATH: a_n] of an infinite series involves [MATH: n]th powers, we can determine whether the series converges or diverges using the root test.

Content:
Suppose we have a series [MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{n =1} ^\infty a_n] such that [MATH: a_n \geq 0] for all [MATH: n \geq 1]. We define [MATH: L] as the following limit:
[MATH: L = \lim_{n \to \infty}\sqrt [n] {a_n} = \lim_{n \to \infty}\left({a_n}\right)^{1/n}]

Content:
Then, the root test states the following:

Content:
- if [MATH: L < 1], the series converges.
- if [MATH: L >1] or [MATH: L = \infty], the series diverges.
- if [MATH: L = 1], the root test is inconclusive.

Content:
Let's use the root test to show that the following geometric series converges:

Content:
[MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{n=1}^\infty \dfrac {1 } {2^n}]

Content:
In this case, our sequence [MATH: a_n] is defined as

Content:
[MATH: a_n = \dfrac{1}{2^n}, \qquad n\geq 1.]

Content:
To apply the root test, we calculate the limit of [MATH: \sqrt[n]{a_n}] as [MATH: n\to\infty{:}]

Content:
[MATH: L|= lim_(n → ∞)root((1)/(2^{n}), n); = lim_(n → ∞)(root(1, n))/(root(2^{n}, n)); = lim_(n → ∞)(1)/(2); = (1)/(2)]

Content:
Since [MATH: L=\dfrac12 < 1,] our series converges by the root test.

Content:
Finally, when applying the root test, it's worth bearing the following limit facts in mind:

Content:
- [MATH: \displaystyle \lim_{n \to \infty } \sqrt [n] {a} = 1] for [MATH: a > 0]
- [MATH: \displaystyle \lim_{n \to \infty } \sqrt [n] {n} = 1]
- [MATH: \displaystyle \lim_{n \to \infty } \sqrt [n] {\dfrac 1 {n!}} = 0]

sections.normalized_html: Use the root test to show that the following series is convergent. [MATH: \sum_{n=1}^\infty \dfrac {(7n)^n n} {(8n + 1) ^ n}]
sections.readable_text:
Use the root test to show that the following series is convergent.
[MATH: \sum_{n=1}^\infty \dfrac {(7n)^n n} {(8n + 1) ^ n}]

sections.normalized_html:
Suppose we have the series [MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{n =1} ^\infty a_n] such that [MATH: a_n \geq 0] for all [MATH: n \geq 1,] and that [MATH: L] is defined as

[MATH: L = \lim_{n \to \infty}\sqrt [n] {a_n} = \lim_{n \to \infty}\left({a_n}\right)^{1/n}.]

Then, the root test states the following:

  • If [MATH: L\lt 1], the series converges.

  • If [MATH: L \gt 1] or [MATH: L = \infty], the series diverges.

  • If [MATH: L = 1], the root test is inconclusive.

We have the sequence [MATH: a_n,] defined as

[MATH: a_n = \dfrac {(7n)^n n} {(8n + 1) ^ n}.]

To apply the root test, we find the limit of [MATH: \sqrt[n]{a_n}] as [MATH: n\to\infty\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: L|= lim_(n → ∞)root(a_{n}, n); = lim_(n → ∞)(a_{n})^{1/n}; = lim_(n → ∞)[((7n)^{n}n)/((8n + 1)^{n})]^{1/n}; = lim_(n → ∞)(7n ⋅ root(n, n))/(8n + 1); = lim_(n → ∞)(((7n ⋅ root(n, n))/(n)))/(((8n)/(n) + (1)/(n))); = lim_(n → ∞)(7root(n, n))/((8 + (1)/(n))); = (7 ⋅ 1)/(8 + 0); = (7)/(8)] Note that we used the fact that

[MATH: \lim_{n\to\infty} \sqrt[n]{n}=1.]

Since [MATH: L =\dfrac{7}{8} \lt 1,] the series converges by the root test.

Item 5 — Example: Applying the Root Test in Divergent and Inconclusive Cases

Example Prompt:

[MATH: \sum_{n=1}^\infty \dfrac{n^45^n}{3^n}]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Suppose we have the series [MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{n =1} ^\infty a_n] such that [MATH: a_n \geq 0] for all [MATH: n \geq 1,] and that [MATH: L] is defined as

[MATH: L = \lim_{n \to \infty}\sqrt [n] {a_n} = \lim_{n \to \infty}\left({a_n}\right)^{1/n}.]

Then, the root test states the following:

- If [MATH: L \lt 1], the series converges.
- If [MATH: L \gt 1] or [MATH: L = \infty], the series diverges.
- If [MATH: L = 1], the root test is inconclusive.

We have the sequence [MATH: a_n,] defined as

[MATH: a_n = \dfrac{n^45^n}{3^n}.]

To apply the root test, we find the limit of [MATH: \sqrt[n]{a_n}] as [MATH: n\to\infty\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: L|= lim_(n → ∞)root(a_{n}, n); = lim_(n → ∞)(a_{n})^{1/n}; = lim_(n → ∞)((n^{4}5^{n})/(3^{n}))^{1/n}; = lim_(n → ∞)((root(n^{4}, n) ⋅ 5)/(3)); = (5)/(3)lim_(n → ∞)root(n^{4}, n); = (5)/(3) ⋅ 1^{4}; = (5)/(3)]

Note that we used the fact that

[MATH: \lim_{n\to\infty} \sqrt[n]{n} = 1.]

Since [MATH: L =\dfrac{5}{3} \gt 1,] the series diverges by the root test.
